dossier.public_summary: The signal is on-target and flat-bottomed with no odd/even difference, but it shows a second eclipse as deep as the first and a strong phase-curve swing nearly as large as the eclipses. The duration is much longer than a planet transit would be around this small star. Together this is a short-period grazing eclipsing binary on the target, not a planet.

reasons.why: Very high-SNR secondary at phase 0.5167 (depth_ppm 3608 vs dip 4096, depth_over_dip 0.8767) is stellar eclipse, not planetary occultation; best_brightening_snr 23.07 does not explain it.
Out-of-eclipse swing is 1.307x dip depth with chi2 858/dof 9, indicating ellipsoidal/beaming from a close stellar companion.
Observed duration 1.234 h vs central_h 0.6864 (ratio 1.797) is far too long for central transit of a 1.74 Re planet around a 0.2478 Rsun M dwarf; stellar companion geometry explains long duration.
Fit density mismatch (star_density_penalty 1006 share 0.6355) shows dip shape is inconsistent with stellar density, as expected for grazing EB.
Difference imaging places dip on target (offset_arcsec 0.5046 err 1.626 sigma 0.3104) and rules out neighbours (closest suspects >10.9 sigma away), so the eclipsing binary is on-target, not a blend.
ML planet score 0.1 is in planet-false positive tail, consistent with binary indicators above.
